peer assessment = students judging one another's work against shared criteria
self-assessment = judging your own work or skills against a standard
open-book exam = a test in which you may use notes or textbooks
sit an exam = to take a formal test
distinction = the highest pass band on some courses and vocational awards
merit = a high pass band below distinction on some awards
appeal a grade = to formally ask for a mark to be reviewed
predicted grade = the result a teacher expects you to achieve in a public exam
school league table = a published ranking of schools by exam results
standardised test = an exam given in the same way so scores can be compared
oral presentation = a short spoken report, often with slides, assessed for content and delivery
fail a module = to not reach the pass mark for a unit of a course
conditional offer = a university place that depends on achieving set exam grades
clearing = the British process matching leftover university places to students after results
tuition fees = the money charged by a university for teaching
scholarship = money given to a student on merit or need to help pay for study
campus = the grounds and buildings of a university or college
undergraduate = a student studying for a first degree, or that level of study
postgraduate = a student studying after a first degree, or that level of study
dissertation = a long piece of original written work at the end of a degree
